chapters.title: Start here: ideas and bits
chapters.summary: See what a computer is doing in plain language, then play with on and off as numbers and a row of bits. No code yet, just motion and cause and effect.
chapters.connection: Strong intro courses start with how you break a problem into steps and what it means for a machine to remember values. We skip syntax on purpose so those habits land before the keyboard gets noisy.

chapters.title: From gates to fetch
chapters.summary: Wire real logic, chain it into addition, then watch a tiny CPU pull an instruction apart. Each step answers why the next one exists.
chapters.connection: This is the same story MIT tells when it moves from Boolean logic up to a real instruction set. When you have seen gates and fetch in miniature, memory, caches, and compilers later feel like upgrades to a story you already know.

chapters.title: Cables and the planet
chapters.summary: Lay links on a map and place a data centre. Distance and cost show up visually, so “where work runs” stops being a vague cloud metaphor.
chapters.connection: Systems courses ask you to reason about latency, failure, and where state lives. A map makes the tradeoffs obvious before you meet routing tables and TCP in depth.

chapters.title: Neural intuition
chapters.summary: Play with attention between toy words, then contrast training weights with answering a prompt. Honest scope: gut feeling first, equations later.
chapters.connection: Modern ML sits on linear algebra and probability, but you still deserve a concrete picture of what training changes versus what inference reuses. This track is that picture.

lessons.title: Computers, binary, and a byte on a wire
lessons.description: Tap the diagram, flip switches, and watch a byte travel. Short notes appear next to what you touch so jargon never runs ahead of the picture.
lessons.connection: Later, when someone says “memory” or “instruction,” you will picture signals moving and storage holding patterns. That image is the payoff of this lesson.

lessons.title: Logic, addition, then fetch
lessons.description: You drive inputs, watch lines light up, then open a toy CPU on fetch and decode. Saves live in this browser so you can leave and come back.
lessons.connection: Real CPUs add more pipeline stages and caches, but fetch and decode never disappear. Here you learn the rhythm once, slowly enough to see it.

steps.title: Build a one bit full adder

lessons.title: Connect the map
lessons.description: Click regions, string cables, drop a data centre. Geography is simplified; the feeling of linking places is not.
lessons.connection: Distributed systems thinking starts with asking where bits live and how far they travel. This lab gives you a physical metaphor before you meet queues, replicas, and consensus.

lessons.title: Transformer intuition
lessons.description: See tokens pay attention to each other, then compare long training runs with a quick answer pass. The goal is intuition, not a substitute for coursework.
lessons.connection: Courses in statistical learning spend weeks on loss and gradients. You get a visual anchor first so those symbols have somewhere to land.
